info.text:
Stocks once fell 89% and took 25 years to get back, or so the story goes. We walk through the world's biggest financial crises, from the Panic of 1907 and the 1929 crash to Black Monday, Japan's bubble, the 1997 Asian currency crisis, 2008 and the 2023 run on Silicon Valley Bank. With real data on unemployment, bank failures and recovery times, we show the pattern every crisis follows and the rules each one left behind, from the Fed to FDIC insurance and circuit breakers.

0:00 Intro
0:41 A panic with no Fed
1:35 The big one: 1929
4:12 The one-day crash
5:15 Bubbles in Asia
7:03 From 2008 to 2023
9:15 The pattern

Sources: Federal Reserve History (Stock Market Crash of 1929; The Great Depression; The Great Recession); Federal Reserve press release, Dec. 16, 2008; Ben Bernanke remarks, Nov. 8, 2002; Federal Reserve review of SVB, Apr. 28, 2023; BLS unemployment data (1929-1940 reconstruction; 2007-2011 annual averages); FDIC history and insured-deposits guide (2026); NY Fed Liberty Street Economics, Nov. 2016; Library of Congress (Black Monday 1987); NYSE market-wide circuit breaker FAQ; Bank of Japan IMES paper; Nikkei Indexes; AP, Feb. 22, 2024; Jiji/Nippon.com, Dec. 30, 2025; Bank of Thailand; Congressional Research Service report on the 1997-98 Asian crisis; Mark Hulbert via History News Network (2009).

News and education, not financial advice.
